Subject: ACME discovery — latency & throughput benchmarks (recap + attachments)

Hi Alex / Jamie —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery:
- Primary workload: chat-like conversational assistant (~1.2k tokens / session average)
- Peak concurrency target: ~200 concurrent sessions for Q3 pilot
- Latency SLO goal: p95 < 250ms for short responses, p99 < 800ms for long tails
- Throughput: need predictable token/sec at scale, with burst tolerance during promotions

Attached are the benchmark artifacts we discussed: acme-latency-throughput-20260622.pdf (end-to-end latency matrices across model variants) and an initial CSV export of token throughput profiles. Nikhil also included a short notes file on batching tradeoffs.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm the SLA/priority for the pilot (is p95 250ms the right bar?)
2) Share any representative prompt files or volumes (anonymized is fine) so we can run a matched benchmark on your prompts
3) If useful, I can put time on the calendar next week for a short bench walkthrough with Nikhil (15–30m)

If I don’t hear back, I’ll follow up in a few days with a short bump — wanted to make sure you had the artifacts to circulate to infra/security.

Best,

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: ACME benchmarks — additional throughput CSV

Hi Alex — forwarding an updated CSV (redwood-benchmarks-20260625.csv) with batch-size vs latency breakdowns we ran against the prompt archetypes you mentioned on the call. Highlights:
- For the 1.2k token median session, continuous batching with batch size ~8 gives best cost/latency tradeoff; p95 latency stayed under 220ms in our infra for the mid-tier model variant.
- p99 showed the usual tail behavior; we’ve included separate rows with KV-cache warm/cold to illustrate the delta (~150–300ms depending on sequence reuse).
- If you need lower p99, recommendations would be: 1) increase reserved capacity to reduce queueing, or 2) enable the higher-performance variant (small CPU/GPU tradeoff).

I’m happy to jump on a bench walkthrough and run a couple of runs with ACME prompt samples if you can share them (anonymized).

Regards,
Nikhil Sharma
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
